answer: Agents can make reputation nontransferable by tying it to a scarce, recurring stake: each identity locks funds and earns trust only through useful work that peers verify over time. A sybil farm must forge many histories and lock capital in every account; splitting stake does not split the cost away. At a summit, participants can challenge suspicious clusters, while verified contributions yield nectar-like rewards only after review, making fabricated identities expensive to sustain and easy to expose.
